title: 7 Ahn Hyo-seop K-dramas to revisit during “Final Table” - Hashtag Legend Hong Kong

 By Tom Kao October 29, 2026 Ahn Hyo-seop is back on screen, and this time, he's heating things up in the kitchen! In "Final Table," he plays Kang Han, a mysterious and talented chef who has made a name for himself overseas. After an unexpected encounter at a struggling restaurant connected to his past, he becomes its head chef and enters The Table: K-Chef 2026, a high-stakes cooking competition to save it from closure. From charming CEOs and dedicated surgeons to complicated romantic leads, Ahn has shown his versatility across different genres. If you're enjoying "Final Table" and want to see more of him, here are seven K-dramas worth revisiting 
 Business Proposal (2022)
 One of Ahn Hyo-seop's most recognisable roles, Business Proposal sees him playing Kang Tae-moo, a handsome but work-obsessed CEO who unexpectedly falls for his employee Shin Ha-ri (Kim Se-jeong). It all begins when Ha-ri attends a blind date in place of her friend, only to discover that her date is actually her boss. Hoping to escape his grandfather's constant matchmaking, Tae-moo proposes a fake relationship, leaving Ha-ri juggling two identities. Packed with hilarious misunderstandings, romantic tension and plenty of swoon-worthy moments, this lighthearted rom-com remains a fan favourite for good reason.
 Dr. Romantic Seasons 2-3 (2020, 2023)
 Trading office romance for the demanding world of medicine, Ahn Hyo-seop plays Seo Woo-jin, a talented but debt-ridden surgeon in Dr. Romantic . After being blacklisted for exposing medical misconduct, he gets a fresh start at Doldam Hospital under the guidance of the eccentric Dr. Kim (Han Suk-kyu). Across Seasons 2 and 3, Woo-jin gradually grows into a more confident and compassionate doctor while developing feelings for fellow surgeon Cha Eun-jae (Lee Sung-kyung). From hospital politics and life-threatening emergencies to the opening of a new trauma centre, there's never a dull moment at Doldam.

 Sold Out on You (2026)
 Before stepping into the kitchen in Final Table , Ahn Hyo-seop returned to romantic comedy with Sold Out on You . He plays Matthew Lee, a perfectionist mushroom farmer whose peaceful countryside life is turned upside down by Dam Ye-jin (Chae Won-been), a workaholic home-shopping host struggling with insomnia. Desperate to secure an exclusive contract for his rare mushrooms and save her career, Ye-jin refuses to take no for an answer. Their clashing personalities lead to plenty of amusing encounters, but as they spend more time together, an unexpected romance begins to blossom, bringing a little healing along the way.
 A Time Called You (2023)
 For something a little more emotional, A Time Called You takes viewers on a bittersweet journey through love, loss and time travel. Ahn Hyo-seop stars opposite Jeon Yeo-been as Koo Yeon-jun and Nam Si-heon, two men from different timelines. Still grieving her boyfriend's death, Han Jun-hee mysteriously travels back to 1998 through a cassette tape, waking up in the body of high school student Kwon Min-ju. There, she meets Si-heon, who looks exactly like her late boyfriend. As unexpected feelings develop, a mysterious murder case adds another twist to this heartfelt romance.
 Lovers of the Red Sky (2021)
 Taking on historical fantasy, Ahn Hyo-seop stars alongside Kim You-jung in Lovers of the Red Sky . Set in a fictionalised historical era, he plays Ha Ram, a blind palace astrologer who can read the stars while secretly plotting revenge against the royal family. When he reunites with Hong Cheon-gi, a gifted painter with whom he shares a childhood connection, old feelings begin to resurface. However, their budding romance soon becomes entangled in royal power struggles and a dangerous demonic curse. With its magical elements and sweeping love story, this period drama offers something quite different from Ahn's modern-day roles.
 Abyss (2019)
 Mixing fantasy, mystery and romance, Abyss sees Ahn Hyo-seop taking on one of his earlier leading roles opposite Park Bo-young. He plays Cha Min, a wealthy but insecure businessman who unexpectedly dies and is brought back to life with a handsome new appearance, thanks to a magical marble called Abyss. When his childhood friend Go Se-yeon, a prosecutor, is murdered, he uses the same marble to revive her. Now living in completely different bodies, the two team up to track down her killer, only to find themselves caught up in dangerous secrets and unexpected romantic feelings.
 Still 17 (2018)
 Photo: SBS
 Long before becoming a familiar leading man, Ahn Hyo-seop won hearts with his supporting role in Still 17 , also known as Thirty But Seventeen . The heartwarming rom-com follows Woo Seo-ri (Shin Hye-sun), who wakes up from a 13-year coma to discover she's now 30, despite still feeling like a teenager. Ahn plays Yoo Chan, a cheerful high school rowing captain who develops a crush on Seo-ri, unaware that his uncle (Yang Se-jong) has feelings for her too. His charming, youthful performance even earned him Best New Actor at the 2018 SBS Drama Awards.
